reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes PlusToken as a crypto app that accepts cryptocurrency deposits and promises users about ten percent monthly returns through its AI Dog feature. It also directs viewers to register through a website or app and describes multilevel referral-code commissions for recruiting others. The due-diligence disclaimer appears alongside these promotional instructions and return-linked participation claims.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker presents an opportunity for viewers to evaluate, not a verified outcome. He recommends due diligence, says he is not a financial advisor, and directs viewers to a longer webinar to understand the proposal. He also distinguishes a reported average from what the program says it promises. That language does not prove the offer is sound, but it matters when deciding whether this video presents an unqualified guarantee rather than investment commentary.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited monthly figure is part of the speaker's account of the program, not proof that a viewer received that return. His registration explanation also says participation is a choice. The referral structure is real content, but the opening does not address his express instruction to investigate before deciding. Those qualifications leave room to read the video as commentary on an opportunity, even if its claims warrant skepticism.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not change what the speaker asks viewers to consider doing. He describes putting crypto into the app's AI Dog for approximately ten percent monthly earnings, urges viewers to act while the opportunity is early, and offers help getting into it. The video promotes participation in a return-generating arrangement; it does not merely discuss market uncertainty.

opening.argument: Much of the presentation is an operational walkthrough. The speaker explains that the wallet is accessed through a phone, points viewers to an installation video, and describes the app's asset area. He even says he has not yet earned anything from the crypto he placed in the AI Dog. A judge can recognize the return claims as claims while treating the walkthrough as a demonstration of how the app is presented and used, rather than evidence that the speaker has independently established those returns.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies return and referral claims, but it treats the tutorial as incidental. The speaker spends time on app access, registration, activation and withdrawals, and acknowledges that his own account has not yet generated earnings. Showing how an interface works does not verify the advertised yield; it can also be read as the video's central explanatory purpose.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is a route into participation, not a neutral software lesson. The speaker recommends the setup videos, explains that activation lets viewers participate in the claimed profits, and says his registration code gives him credit for commissions. His lack of personal earnings does not neutralize those instructions or the claimed monthly return.

opening.argument: The described product is a mobile crypto wallet with ordinary account functions alongside its earnings pitch. The speaker says users receive a recovery seed, can withdraw without a contract or minimum withdrawal, and do not need a sponsor to earn. He also describes wallet addresses, exchange records and settings. Those are claims, not proof that the service works as advertised. But the video does not itself demonstrate that funds become inaccessible or that recruitment is required to use the product. The visible evidence permits a reading of a wallet-service promotion whose claims need checking, rather than a demonstrated loss of user control.

records of exchange you can add your wallet addresses over here settings contact us

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's quotes establish that the speaker describes an AI Dog return and ten referral levels. They do not establish that withdrawals fail or that a recruit is necessary for a user to receive the stated wallet earnings. The speaker explicitly separates the no-sponsor offer from team-building commissions. That distinction does not validate the returns, but it limits what the referral evidence alone can prove.

you can withdraw your funds at any time you're not locked into a contract or anything of the sort

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A video need not show failed withdrawals to promote this arrangement. The speaker tells viewers to put crypto into the app's AI Dog for an approximate monthly return, specifies a minimum amount, and explains commissions tied to referrals' earnings. Wallet features and asserted withdrawal rights do not remove the funded-return mechanism that the video urges viewers to join.
